themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints in Sunnyside/Woodside spiked to 18 this week—167% above the 8-week average of 6.8 per week—signaling a rapid escalation in environmental violations and street quality degradation in the past 7 days.
evidence: 18 illegal dumping complaints this week vs. 6.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.34)
167% spike represents statistically significant deviation (severity: high)
Timing: newest spike in dataset, emerged within last 7 days
reporting_angles: On-the-ground reporting: which blocks/corridors are dumping hotspots and why are residents not reporting faster?
Sanitation Department responsiveness: what is typical remediation timeline for illegal dumping in this district?

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 4 this week—967% above the 8-week baseline of 0.4 per week—suggesting emerging friction over sidewalk seating, possibly tied to recent seasonal reopenings or enforcement gaps in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.49)
Suggests either new venue activity, sidewalk obstruction issues, or ADA/pedestrian access complaints
reporting_angles: Identify which outdoor dining venues or corridors are triggering complaints—are there specific restaurants or blocks?
How does this compare to permit approval timeline and enforcement activity by Department of Consumer Affairs?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 36 last week—476% above the 8-week average of 6.2 per week—indicating a sharp rise in unhoused populations or visible street-level encampments over the past 1–2 weeks.
evidence: 36 encampment complaints last week vs. 6.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.43)
476% spike is one of the largest in dataset, sustained within past 1–2 weeks
Overlaps with broader citywide homelessness trends and NYC's shelter system capacity issues
reporting_angles: Street-level reporting: where are the largest/newest encampments in Sunnyside/Woodside and what services/outreach are available?
Policy angle: how is NYC Department of Homeless Services responding to the spike, and is community board requesting additional outreach resources?

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 14 last week—918% above the 8-week average of 1.4 per week—indicating rapid infrastructure wear, pothole formation, or ADA compliance issues on neighborhood streets over the past 7–14 days.
evidence: 14 curb condition complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.63)
918% spike represents one of highest z-scores in dataset, emerged within past 7–14 days
Aligns with ongoing Street Condition complaints (1,232 over 90 days) suggesting broader pavement/curb maintenance gap
reporting_angles: Identify worst-affected streets or intersections—are there patterns (e.g., heavy truck routes, aging infrastructure)?
NYCDOT repair backlog: how long is typical timeline for curb restoration in CD 402 vs. citywide average?

themes_detail.label: Site Safety & Building Concerns
themes_detail.summary: BEST/Site Safety complaints spiked dramatically—2,300% above the 8-week average of 0.1 per week (3 complaints 2 weeks ago)—flagging potential construction hazards, unsafe scaffolding, or building code violations in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 3 BEST/Site Safety complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
2,300% spike is the highest in dataset by percentage, emerged 2 weeks ago
656 DOB permit filings in past 90 days (448 alterations, 106 new buildings, 16 demolitions) suggest active construction activity driving hazard complaints
reporting_angles: Match 311 complaints to DOB filings: which construction sites or alterations are generating safety violations?
Interview FDNY or DOB enforcement: are there patterns of non-compliance or repeat violations at specific sites?
